correctness.rationale: The condition \(r_i+c_j-2x_{ij}\ge3\) is equivalent to three distinct selected open neighbors. Every row must have at least two cells; any row with two forces two full columns and no empty columns. Hence 6 only for \(n=2\), 8 only n=3,4 and at least 9 for \(n\ge5\). Nine-cell solutions either have one two-row, forcing the unique \(n=5\) exceptional configuration, or row sums (3,3,3) with column profiles (3,3,3) or (3,2,2,2), the latter having omitted-row bijection. All structures are checked for sufficiency and counted with disjoint cases. Graph-level exhaustive \(n=2\)..7 and independent type-multiset n=8..12 tests agree. Finite tests do not certify the infinite theorem; the row/column argument supplies its proof.

value.rationale: The minimum size on this natural infinite graph family is known but does not characterize or count extremizers. The result exactly identifies all extremal sets for every \(n\ge2\), including a genuine five-column structural exception, with a quartic multiplicity formula n>=6. Since \(K_3\square K_n\) is the line graph of K_{3,n}, this also describes minimum incident-edge monitoring configurations; the labeled count gives the leading coefficient in independent-activation reliability. This is an infinite classification on a motivated parameter, not merely a finite instance or a cosmetic parameter substitution.
